findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded as plaintext Lambda environment variables in the Terraform file. They are stored unencrypted in state, visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunction or repository access, and grant whatever permissions the IAM user holds.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the function's environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in plaintext by any principal able to describe the function.
No tracing_config block is defined, so request tracing is disabled and forensic reconstruction of an attack against the function is not possible.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a runtime that has reached end of support and no longer receives security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.
The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control callbacks if the code is compromised.
